text: In the statistical multiplexing example, 100 users at 5% activity are served by a 20 Mb/s link with what approximate overflow probability?
explanation: The binomial calculation with n=100, p=0.05 gives a probability under 10^-6 that more than 20 users are simultaneously active. One fifth of the circuit-switched capacity, essentially the same service — and that factor, compounded at every level of aggregation, is why packet switching won.
